title: Abortion
reason: A deeply polarized moral issue with no cross-spectrum consensus position; including it in any form would immediately code the platform as partisan.

title: Voting Rights
reason: Currently coded as a partisan battleground — the access-versus-integrity framing splits cleanly along party lines. It fails the bipartisan test for now.

title: Supreme Court Expansion
reason: Not bipartisan enough. Judicial term limits and ethics rules remain targets — see the Term Limits and Ethics amendments.

title: Civic Information & Informed Citizenry
reason: A great idea for a new company or non-profit, but it doesn't yet meet the bar for popular support behind a constitutional amendment.

title: Presidential Self-Pardon Ban
reason: Not bipartisan enough — support splits 82% among Democrats and 43% among Republicans. Pardon transparency and public-benefit limits remain a target — see Pardon Reform.

title: Eliminate Qualified Immunity for Policing
reason: The weakest bipartisan case of the original targets: Republican support for elimination is only 39–46% in every credible poll, and the data is stale (2020–21). Could return if reframed around officer accountability — that framing polls at 84% overall — and validated with fresh polling.

title: Balanced Budget
reason: Strong but shallow: 69–80% support in the abstract, collapsing to 31% in the one trade-off experiment ever run once entitlement cuts are specified. Democrats defect on benefit cuts, Republicans on tax increases.
